mt-bethel-church-marietta-ga-independent.assessment: Mt. Bethel Church Marietta GA is one of the most prominent post-UMC independent megachurches. Senior Pastor Dr. Jody Ray (since 2016) was reassigned by UMC Bishop Sue Haupert-Johnson in 2021; he surrendered his UMC clergy credentials in protest, the congregation gathered ~4,700 signatures, and the church ultimately paid ~$13.1M in a 2022 settlement to leave the UMC with property. Importantly, Mt. Bethel did NOT join the GMC — it operates as an independent Methodist congregation. ~10,000 members, 2,300+ avg attendance. The pastor's and congregation's deliberate stand against UMC progressive leadership is theologically substantive. Yellow denominational reflects post-schism independence with no connectional accountability — the autonomy is sometimes a weakness, sometimes a strength.

mt-horeb-lexington-sc-gmc.assessment: Mt. Horeb Church in Lexington, SC was South Carolina's largest United Methodist congregation before a dramatic 97% congregational vote on February 26, 2023 to leave the UMC, with formal GMC membership finalized in August 2023. Senior Pastor Jeff Kersey has led through this transition. The church runs two campuses (East traditional, West contemporary) with four services total each Sunday morning, and emphasizes making, maturing, and mobilizing disciples. Like all post-2022 GMC churches, the institutional commitment to orthodoxy (evidenced by the costly decision to leave UMC property and structure) is the strongest signal — these are congregations that paid a price to preserve biblical teaching on marriage and Christian doctrine. The GMC South Carolina Conference position on women as elders should be verified; otherwise this is a solidly orthodox Wesleyan option in the Columbia metro area.
